title: Natural Domain of a Radical Denominator
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine the natural domain of the function f(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{x^2 - 5x + 6}}. Use interval notation to state your final answer.
hints: Note the dual restriction: the expression is inside an even root (requiring non-negativity) AND in a denominator (forbidding zero).
Combine both conditions into a single strict inequality: x^2 - 5x + 6 > 0.
Factor the quadratic expression and construct a sign chart across the resulting intervals.

steps.title: Combine Radical and Denominator Restrictions
steps.explanation: Because the radical is situated in the denominator, the radicand must be strictly positive: non-negative for the square root, and non-zero to avoid division by zero.
steps.why: Radicals in denominators require strict positivity (strictly greater than zero) rather than non-negativity.

steps.title: Factor the Quadratic Radicand
steps.explanation: Find two numbers whose product is 6 and sum is -5, yielding the factorization (x - 2)(x - 3).
steps.why: Factoring determines the critical transition numbers x = 2 and x = 3.

steps.title: Construct a Sign Chart
steps.explanation: The numbers 2 and 3 divide the real line into three intervals: (-inf, 2), (2, 3), and (3, inf). On (-inf, 2), both factors are negative, giving a positive product. On (2, 3), the factors have opposite signs, giving a negative product. On (3, inf), both factors are positive, giving a positive product. We select the strictly positive intervals.
steps.why: A continuous polynomial changes sign only at its real roots.

steps.title: State the Domain with Strict Endpoints
steps.explanation: Because x = 2 and x = 3 cause the denominator to equal zero, both endpoints must be excluded using open parentheses.
steps.why: Division by zero is undefined, strictly excluding the boundary roots.
